sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的蕾切尔·阿布拉姆斯，这是《每日》栏目。

sentences.en: I run through this execution every day in my heart.
sentences.zh: 我每天都在心中演练这个行刑过程。

sentences.en: Last week, a Tennessee woman named Krista Pike was set to be executed by lethal injection.
sentences.zh: 上周，田纳西州一名叫克丽丝塔·派克的女子原本要接受注射死刑。

sentences.en: The concerns I have on our lethal injection method are simply that I do not have good things.
sentences.zh: 我对我们的注射死刑方法感到担忧，简单来说就是没有什么好结果。

sentences.en: In the days leading up to her planned execution, Pike told my colleague Emily Cochran about her fears of the state's ability to kill her without complication.
sentences.zh: 在她计划行刑前的几天里，派克向我的同事埃米莉·科克伦讲述了她对该州能否毫无意外地将她处死的恐惧。

sentences.en: The drug was very bad.
sentences.zh: 这种药非常糟糕。

sentences.en: In the end, Pike survived two doses of a lethal injection drug and regained consciousness in a Nashville hospital where her condition remained severe.
sentences.zh: 最后，派克挺过了两剂死刑药物，并在纳什维尔的一家医院恢复了意识，其间她的情况依然严重。

sentences.en: And on top of that, this was Tennessee's second botched execution in just a few months and has led the governor to pause executions for the remainder of the year.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，这是田纳西州在短短几个月内的第二次行刑失误，并导致州长暂停了今年剩余时间的死刑执行。

sentences.en: Today, Pamela Koloff talks about the waning public support for the death penalty and why, despite it, some states are still doubling down.
sentences.zh: 今天，帕梅拉·科洛夫将探讨公众对死刑支持率的下降，以及为什么尽管如此，一些州仍在加倍坚持死刑。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, October 8th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月8日，星期四。

sentences.en: Pam Koloff, welcome to The Daily.
sentences.zh: 帕姆·科洛夫，欢迎来到《每日》。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: So, Pam, I think a lot of people have been really stunned by the Krista Pike case.
sentences.zh: 那么，帕姆，我想很多人都被克丽丝塔·派克案震惊了。

sentences.en: And Krista Pike, of course, is this woman who confessed to and was convicted of a really gruesome murder back in the 90s.
sentences.zh: 当然，克丽丝塔·派克就是那个在90年代承认并被判犯下极其骇人谋杀罪的女子。

sentences.en: But that obviously is not what people are talking about this last week.
sentences.zh: 但显然这并不是过去一周人们在谈论的事情。

sentences.en: What people are focused on are the really grisly details of this botched execution attempt of Krista Pike in Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 人们关注的是田纳西州对克丽丝塔·派克这次行刑失败中极其毛骨悚然的细节。

sentences.en: This execution attempt has really ignited this national conversation about the death penalty, how we do it, why we do it.
sentences.zh: 这次行刑未遂确实点燃了全国关于死刑的讨论：我们如何执行，为什么要执行。

sentences.en: And we wanted to talk to you because you are a reporter who has covered the death penalty for years.
sentences.zh: 我们想和你聊聊，因为你是一位报道死刑多年的记者。

sentences.en: You recently wrote a book about it called Catch the Devil.
sentences.zh: 你最近写了一本关于它的书，名叫《抓住恶魔》。

sentences.en: So tell us what your reaction to this case has been and where you think it fits into the broader conversation that we're having right now about the death penalty in America in this
sentences.zh: 所以请告诉我们，你对这个案子的反应是什么，你认为它如何契合我们现在关于美国死刑的广泛讨论，在这个

sentences.en: moment.
sentences.zh: 时刻。

sentences.en: I think when we look at what happened to Krista Pike, who, to be clear, survived lethal injection,
sentences.zh: 我想当我们看到克丽丝塔·派克遭遇了什么——需要明确的是，她从注射死刑中活了下来，

sentences.en: which is something we are not familiar with having happened and sort of lays bare the gruesomeness
sentences.zh: 这是我们不曾熟悉发生过的事情，某种程度上赤裸裸地展现了

sentences.en: of the task at hand, we can see that this is sort of the worst example of something that's been building and building and that I think sort of finally broke through to people who
sentences.zh: 这项任务的残酷性，我们可以看到，这某种程度上是一系列不断累积的问题中最糟糕的例子，我认为它最终触动了那些

sentences.en: don't spend all their time, like me, wondering why it is that we do this and why we do it the way we do it.
sentences.zh: 不会像我一样把所有时间都花在思考“我们为什么要这样做”以及“为什么我们要以这种方式这样做”的人。

sentences.en: There have been so many issues for the past few years with lethal injection.
sentences.zh: 过去几年里，注射死刑出现了如此多的问题。

sentences.en: There was another botched execution in Tennessee with a completely different issue in May.
sentences.zh: 5月份田纳西州发生了另一起行刑失误，涉及完全不同的问题。

sentences.en: And I think something important to understand is this is happening at a time when support among Americans for capital punishment has taken a nosedive.
sentences.zh: 我认为有一点很重要，那就是发生这一切的时候，美国人对死刑的支持率已经呈断崖式下跌。

sentences.en: We currently have, I think it's just above 50% of Americans who support the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 目前支持死刑的美国人比例，我想大概刚过50%多一点。

sentences.en: And so these questions are percolating to the surface in a way that they weren't back in the 1980s and 1990s.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些问题正在浮出水面，这是上世纪80和90年代所没有的。

sentences.en: But what's interesting is while we have a decline in public support, we have these outlier states,
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，在公众支持率下降的同时，我们也有一些持极端立场的州，

sentences.en: Tennessee being one of them, that are executing more people than they have in recent years.
sentences.zh: 田纳西州就是其中之一，他们处决的人数比近年来还要多。

sentences.en: So I want to get into the reasons why some states might be doubling down in this moment.
sentences.zh: 所以我想探讨一下为什么有些州在此时此刻可能会加倍坚持死刑。

sentences.en: But first, I just want to understand the history of that declining public support.
sentences.zh: 但首先，我只想了解这种公众支持率下降的历史。

sentences.en: Where would you start that story and how would you tell it?
sentences.zh: 你会从哪里开始讲这个故事，又会如何讲述它？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it goes back to the 1980s and to the tough on crime era.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这可以追溯到20世纪80年代的严厉打击犯罪时代。

sentences.en: Crime is on the increase in the United States.
sentences.zh: 美国的犯罪率当时在上升。

sentences.en: There was such a degree of violent crime at that time that we have trouble imagining now.
sentences.zh: 当时暴力犯罪的程度是我们现在难以想象的。

sentences.en: In 1980, nearly 5 million households were touched by rape, robbery, or assault.
sentences.zh: 1980年，近500万家庭遭遇了强奸、抢劫或袭击。

sentences.en: It was more than twice the rate of violent crime then, in the 80s and early 90s.
sentences.zh: 当时暴力犯罪率是80年代和90年代初的两倍多。

sentences.en: It's the same story everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到处都是一样的情况。

sentences.en: The fear.
sentences.zh: 恐惧。

sentences.en: People are afraid to leave their houses.
sentences.zh: 人们害怕离开家门。

sentences.en: People are afraid and looking for ways to fight back.
sentences.zh: 人们感到害怕，并寻找反击的方法。

sentences.en: And so people were looking for answers to how do we get control of what's going on?
sentences.zh: 因此，人们在寻找答案：我们如何控制正在发生的事情？

sentences.en: How do we feel safe again?
sentences.zh: 我们如何才能重新感到安全？

sentences.en: And the death penalty seemed like an answer.
sentences.zh: 死刑似乎是一个答案。

sentences.en: The death penalty seemed like an answer.
sentences.zh: 死刑似乎是一个答案。

sentences.en: Long sentences seemed like an answer.
sentences.zh: 重判似乎是一个答案。

sentences.en: Just a much harsher approach.
sentences.zh: 只是一种严厉得多的方法。

sentences.en: You know, there was so much both real fear and a lot of fear-mongering on the part of politicians.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当时既有真实的恐惧，也有政客们煽动的大量恐惧。

sentences.en: It was very, very politically expedient to be pro-death penalty, to use all that language.
sentences.zh: 主张死刑、使用所有这些言论在政治上非常非常有利可图。

sentences.en: We had hundreds of death sentences being handed down during that period, hundreds of executions.
sentences.zh: 在那段时期，我们有数百起死刑判决下达，数百次死刑执行。

sentences.en: And just to remind us, Pam, in this period in the 80s and 90s that you're talking about, was lethal injection the main way that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 顺便提醒一下，帕姆，在你谈到的80和90年代这段时期，注射死刑是美国

sentences.en: executed people?
sentences.zh: 处决犯人的主要方式吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, this was the era of the modern, supposedly humane execution.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是现代所谓的人道主义行刑的时代。

sentences.en: Yesterday, Oklahoma Governor Boren signed into law a bill providing for execution by intravenous injections of a quick-acting drug.
sentences.zh: 昨天，俄克拉荷马州州长博伦签署了一项法律，规定通过静脉注射速效药物执行死刑。

sentences.en: Lethal injection was developed as a method in Oklahoma in 1977.
sentences.zh: 注射死刑作为一种方法于1977年在俄克拉荷马州开发出来。

sentences.en: The bill's sponsor, Ben Z.
sentences.zh: 该法案的发起人本·Z·

sentences.en: Grant, says the new method will do away with the more brutal aspects of the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 格兰特表示，新方法将消除死刑中更残酷的方面。

sentences.en: Texas was the first state to use it in 1982 when a man named Charlie Brooks was put to death.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州是1982年第一个使用该方法的州，当时一个名叫查理·布鲁克斯的人被处决。

sentences.en: Brooks sat in his cell, his plain cell, all day long waiting.
sentences.zh: 布鲁克斯一整天都坐在他的牢房里，他简陋的牢房里等待着。

sentences.en: He had three visitors, two Muslim chaplains, and his niece, Barry Mitchell.
sentences.zh: 他有三位访客，两位穆斯林教士和他的侄女巴里·米切尔。

sentences.en: But at 6 p.m., the visitors were let out.
sentences.zh: 但在下午6点，访客被请了出去。

sentences.en: Brooks was given his final shower and ate his final meal, T-bone steak, french fries, and peach cobbler.
sentences.zh: 布鲁克斯进行了最后一次淋浴，并吃了他的最后一餐：T骨牛排、炸薯条和桃子脆皮饼。

sentences.en: And that marked this new era where states began to shift to lethal injection.
sentences.zh: 这标志着一个新时代的开始，各州开始转向注射死刑。

sentences.en: The idea was that lethal injection was more humane.
sentences.zh: 当时的理念是注射死刑更加人道。

sentences.en: More humane than like the electric chair or some of these other methods that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 比电椅或美国一直在使用的其他一些方法更人道。

sentences.en: had been using.
sentences.zh: 一直都在使用。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Less barbaric.
sentences.zh: 没那么野蛮。

sentences.en: And so the introduction of lethal injection, I think, made people more comfortable with the practice.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为注射死刑的引入让人们对这种做法感到更加自在。

sentences.en: It looked like a medical procedure.
sentences.zh: 它看起来像是一个医疗程序。

sentences.en: And so I think that coupled with this incredible rise in violent crime made people feel that this was an answer to that problem.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，这加上暴力犯罪的惊人增长，让人们觉得这是解决那个问题的答案。

sentences.en: That leads to this sort of high-water mark of public support for capital punishment.
sentences.zh: 这导致了公众对死刑支持率的某种最高峰。

sentences.en: Gallup found that in 1994, 80% of Americans supported capital punishment.
sentences.zh: 盖洛普发现，1994年，80%的美国人支持死刑。

sentences.en: But that support slowly started to erode.
sentences.zh: 但这种支持开始慢慢侵蚀。

sentences.en: Well, that is really interesting because you have a problem, you have a solution that people like, and you have a lot of support for it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这真的很有趣，因为你有一个问题，你有一个人们喜欢的解决方案，你对此有很多支持。

sentences.en: So why would that support start to wane, given all of that?
sentences.zh: 那么鉴于所有这些，为什么这种支持会开始减弱呢？

sentences.en: I think there are a few different things in play.
sentences.zh: 我认为有几个不同的因素在起作用。

sentences.en: I think the most important thing, first of all, was the falling rate of violent crime.
sentences.zh: 首先，我认为最重要的事情是暴力犯罪率的下降。

sentences.en: We can see this sort of precipitous drop that starts in the 90s and then goes through the aughts.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到这种从90年代开始然后贯穿整个2000年代的急剧下降。

sentences.en: And by the time we get to 2012, 2013, we're looking at a crime rate that's roughly half of what it had been just two decades earlier.
sentences.zh: 到了2012年、2013年，我们看到的犯罪率大约只是仅仅二十年前的一半。

sentences.en: So as we see the violent crime rate rapidly decrease,
sentences.zh: 因此，随着暴力犯罪率迅速下降，

sentences.en: I think the urgency of the language around this tough-on-crime ethos and around capital punishment in particular starts to wane in combination with other issues such as the growing costs of these kinds of cases.
sentences.zh: 我认为围绕这种打击犯罪精神以及特别是围绕死刑的言论的紧迫性开始减弱，并结合了其他问题，例如这类案件不断增长的成本。

sentences.en: Growing costs.
sentences.zh: 不断增长的成本。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: Like you're saying it's more expensive to prosecute a capital punishment case or?
sentences.zh: 就像你是说起诉死刑案件更贵，还是？

sentences.en: Much, much, much more expensive.
sentences.zh: 非常、非常、非常昂贵。

sentences.en: And so especially for a rural county with limited resources, when we're talking millions of dollars, which it is every time you do a capital prosecution,
sentences.zh: 因此，特别是对于资源有限的农村县，当我们谈论数百万美元时——每次进行死刑起诉都是如此——

sentences.en: you're talking about taking resources away from many other very important things.
sentences.zh: 你就是在把资源从许多其他非常重要的事情上抽走。

sentences.en: And I think these combination of factors start to erode some public confidence in the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些因素的组合开始侵蚀公众对死刑的一些信心。

sentences.en: So less violent crime means less demand for an urgent solution.
sentences.zh: 所以暴力犯罪减少意味着对紧急解决方案的需求减少。

sentences.en: And also, by the way, these cases have been very, very expensive, and maybe you could put that money towards something else.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这些案件一直非常非常昂贵，也许你可以把这笔钱用在别的地方。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But I think there's a third big reason for the decline in public confidence in the death penalty, and I think it's the most interesting one.
sentences.zh: 但我认为公众对死刑信心下降还有第三个大原因，我认为这是最有趣的一个。

sentences.en: And that is the advent of DNA analysis.
sentences.zh: 那就是DNA分析的出现。

sentences.en: Today, science is on the threshold of a new era.
sentences.zh: 今天，科学正处于新时代的门槛上。

sentences.en: It completely transforms the future of criminal investigations, but it also does something for past convictions,
sentences.zh: 它彻底改变了刑事调查的未来，但它也对过去的定罪起到了某种作用，

sentences.en: because it allows defendants and their attorneys to go back and look at, did prosecutors get it right?
sentences.zh: 因为它允许被告和他们的律师回过头去看看，检方真的做对了吗？

sentences.en: It would not be the first time innocent people were sent to prison for crimes they did not commit.
sentences.zh: 无辜的人因他们未曾犯下的罪行而被送进监狱，这已经不是第一次了。

sentences.en: DNA could be the instrument of vindication.
sentences.zh: DNA可以成为正名工具。

sentences.en: Twice convicted for the murder of a girl in 1984, a Maryland man faced the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 一名马里兰州男子因1984年谋杀一名女孩两次被定罪，面临死刑。

sentences.en: Tonight, though, Kirk Bloodsworth is a free man because of DNA evidence.
sentences.zh: 不过，今晚柯克·布拉德斯沃思因DNA证据成为自由之身。

sentences.en: With DNA analysis, they're able to hold up these old convictions to scrutiny and to see whether the correct person was behind bars.
sentences.zh: 通过DNA分析，他们能够对这些旧的定罪进行审查，看看是否是正确的人被关在铁窗后面。

sentences.en: For 27 years, he was known as inmate number 082629.
sentences.zh: 27年来，他被称为082629号囚犯。

sentences.en: Now, William Dillon, or Bill as his family calls him, is spending time in his mother's backyard.
sentences.zh: 现在，威廉·狄龙——或者他的家人叫他比尔——正在他母亲的后院度过时光。

sentences.en: And that then resulted in a cascade of a tremendous amount of exonerations.
sentences.zh: 这随后导致了大量平反案件的涌现。

sentences.en: It wasn't me.
sentences.zh: 不是我。

sentences.en: That is what Earl Ruffin has said all along after he was charged with raping a woman in the Ghent section of Norfolk.
sentences.zh: 厄尔·鲁芬在被指控在诺福克的根特社区强奸一名妇女后，一直都是这么说的。

sentences.en: It wasn't until DNA evidence weighed in 21 years later that justice was served.
sentences.zh: 直到21年后DNA证据介入，正义才得以伸张。

sentences.en: This is where I think I remember becoming kind of aware of this issue because I remember the Innocence Project in particular getting a lot of attention in this moment.
sentences.zh: 这就是我开始意识到这个问题的地方，因为我记得无罪计划在这个时候特别受到了很多关注。

sentences.en: They took this up as their mission, right?
sentences.zh: 他们把这作为他们的使命，对吧？

sentences.en: Like using DNA to go back to old cases and exonerating a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 就像利用DNA回溯旧案并为很多人平反一样。

sentences.en: And I think that that was probably the first time that people understood that convictions could not be taken as fact.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可能是人们第一次明白定罪不能被当作铁的事实。

sentences.en: And it raised a lot of questions about whether we had been wrongly executing people.
sentences.zh: 它引发了许多关于我们是否一直在错误处决人的疑问。

sentences.en: I think it's hard to even envision now.
sentences.zh: 我想现在甚至很难想象。

sentences.en: But I'll just say that when I started as a reporter in the 90s reporting on the criminal justice system, if you suggested that there were innocent people on death row,
sentences.zh: 但我只想说，当我90年代作为报道刑事司法系统的记者刚开始工作时，如果你暗示死刑犯中有无辜的人，

sentences.en: you were considered a little fringe.
sentences.zh: 你会被认为有点边缘化。

sentences.en: Very much so.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: God, in hindsight, it just feels like that would be so natural to question.
sentences.zh: 天哪，事后看来，质疑这一点似乎是那么自然。

sentences.en: But that's because of so much of what happened in the 90s and beyond.
sentences.zh: 但那是因为90年代及以后发生的很多事情。

sentences.en: So this shift that we see in public consciousness that we just assume has always been there, that we understand that the criminal justice system is highly imperfect,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们看到公众意识的这种转变——我们只是假设它一直存在，我们理解刑事司法系统很不完美——

sentences.en: this brought this into focus in a very, very sharp way.
sentences.zh: 这以一种非常、非常强烈的方式将这一点带入了人们的视线。

sentences.en: And I think especially for populations who hadn't thought about these issues before, this became shocking.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，特别是对于以前没有考虑过这些问题的人群来说，这变得令人震惊。

sentences.en: And every few months, there was a DNA exoneration.
sentences.zh: 每隔几个月，就会有一起通过DNA平反的案件。

sentences.en: We now have, since the early 1970s, over 200 death penalty exonerations.
sentences.zh: 自20世纪70年代初以来，我们现在有超过200起死刑平反案件。

sentences.en: So that's over 200 people who received a death sentence, who went to death row, who now walk free.
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着有200多名被判处死刑、进入死刑牢房、现在重获自由的人。

sentences.en: That's a staggering number.
sentences.zh: 这是一个惊人的数字。

sentences.en: And it's hard to imagine that this system is working well when you know that.
sentences.zh: 当你了解到这一点时，很难想象这个系统运作良好。

sentences.en: And beyond people sort of changing their ideas about capital punishment and faith in the justice system, how did governments respond or did anything else change?
sentences.zh: 除了人们改变对死刑的看法和对司法系统的信心之外，政府是如何反应的，或者还有什么改变吗？

sentences.en: Well, there was sort of a lag period.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有一个滞后期。

sentences.en: I mean, I was very aware as a reporter in the late 1990s of this huge upsurge that we had had where it peaked in 1999 with 98 people being executed that year.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，作为20世纪90年代末的一名记者，我非常清楚这种巨大的激增，它在1999年达到顶峰，当年有98人被处决。

sentences.en: In Texas alone, there were 35 people executed.
sentences.zh: 仅在德克萨斯州，就有35人被处决。

sentences.en: And it was a relentless drumbeat of executions at that time.
sentences.zh: 当时行刑的鼓点是不间断的。

sentences.en: Then, in 2000, Governor George Ryan in Illinois instituted a moratorium on the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 然后，在2000年，伊利诺伊州州长乔治·瑞安暂停了死刑。

sentences.en: And he did so after an incredible Chicago Tribune investigation really showed just how many problems there were with the cases that were on Illinois' death row,
sentences.zh: 而且他之所以这么做，是因为《芝加哥论坛报》进行了一项令人难以置信的调查，真正揭示了伊利诺伊州死囚牢房里的案件存在多少问题，

sentences.en: including 13 men who ended up being innocent.
sentences.zh: 其中包括最终被证明是无辜的 13 名男子。

sentences.en: It would take a while for more things like that to happen.
sentences.zh: 要让更多类似的事情发生还需要一段时间。

sentences.en: But slowly, in the years that followed, more states began to follow suit, putting moratoriums in play or simply just not acting upon the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 但在接下来的几年里，越来越多的州慢慢开始效仿，实行暂停死刑，或者干脆不对死刑采取行动。

sentences.en: And then in 2003, the federal government started this sort of unofficial moratorium.
sentences.zh: 然后在 2003 年，联邦政府开始了这种非官方的暂停死刑。

sentences.en: So they really seem to be taking a cue from what the states are doing.
sentences.zh: 所以他们看起来确实是在效仿各州的做法。

sentences.en: That's what it seems like.
sentences.zh: 情况似乎确实如此。

sentences.en: But obviously, Pam, there are people who still support the death penalty during this period, despite all of these revelations, who do not feel that they should be stopped.
sentences.zh: 但显而易见的是，帕姆，尽管发生了这一切，在这期间仍然有人支持死刑，他们觉得不应该叫停死刑。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And I think that was highly concentrated geographically.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这种现象在地理上高度集中。

sentences.en: But broadly, we can see that the victims' rights movement and prosecutors' associations strongly believed in the death penalty and fought for the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 但总体而言，我们可以看到受害者权利运动和检察官协会坚信死刑并为死刑而战。

sentences.en: But the overall trend across the country was so dramatic.
sentences.zh: 但全国范围内的整体趋势却是如此戏剧性。

sentences.en: What I was seeing on the ground was, was this not the end of the death penalty, but was this a new era that was leading toward the end of death penalty?
sentences.zh: 我在实地看到的情况是，这难道不是死刑的终结，而是一个通往死刑终结的新时代吗？

sentences.en: The beginning of the end.
sentences.zh: 终结的开始。

sentences.en: The beginning of the end of the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 死刑终结的开始。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我编写了《纽约时报》游戏中的拼词游戏 Connections，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，我也喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天都制作 Spelling Bee 和 Letterboxd 这两款游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做色联觉的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚刚听到声音的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com slash games 开始游玩今天的游戏。

sentences.en: Okay, so Pam, talk to us more about what President Trump did to try to encourage use of the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 好的，帕姆，跟我们多聊聊特朗普总统为了鼓励使用死刑都做了什么。

sentences.en: Well, the first really important thing he did was in his first term.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他做的第一件真正重要的事是在他的第一个任期内。

sentences.en: So this was after the federal government had not carried out any executions in 17 years.
sentences.zh: 当时联邦政府已经有 17 年没有执行过任何死刑了。

sentences.en: And Trump restarted them in July of 2020, and there were 13 federal executions in the final six months of his first term.
sentences.zh: 特朗普在 2020 年 7 月重新开始执行死刑，在他第一任期的最后六个月里，联邦执行了 13 次死刑。

sentences.en: So that's a pretty powerful statement about how he feels about the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 所以这对于他对死刑的看法是一个非常强有力的表态。

sentences.en: And I think from there, we can see the seeds of what then happened in his second term.
sentences.zh: 我想从那里开始，我们就能看到他随后在第二任期中所发生事情的萌芽。

sentences.en: On his very first day back into office, January 20th of 2025, he signed a sweeping executive order, which was called Restoring the Death Penalty and Protecting Public Safety.
sentences.zh: 在他重返白宫的第一天，即 2025 年 1 月 20 日，他签署了一项广泛的行政令，名为《恢复死刑和保护公共安全》。

sentences.en: Okay, very explicit.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常明确。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this really signaled to everyone that he was doubling down on the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 这向所有人发出了一个明确的信号，即他在死刑问题上在加码。

sentences.en: At this time, that it's ebbing everywhere else.
sentences.zh: 而在此时，死刑在其他地方正在消退。

sentences.en: And so he did everything from instructing the attorney general to pursue death sentences more aggressively,
sentences.zh: 因此，他采取了一系列措施，从指示总检察长更加积极地寻求死刑判决，

sentences.en: calling on the Justice Department to challenge the Supreme Court decisions that limited the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 到呼吁司法部挑战限制死刑的最高法院裁决。

sentences.en: And I think most significantly, you know, he does not control state district attorneys' offices,
sentences.zh: 我认为最重要的是，你知道的，他无法控制各州的地区检察官办公室，

sentences.en: but he made clear that he wanted them to seek the death penalty as often as they possibly could.
sentences.zh: 但他明确表示，他希望他们尽可能频繁地寻求死刑。

sentences.en: He was doubling down on it.
sentences.zh: 他在死刑问题上加倍下注。

sentences.en: He was trying to send a message to the states.
sentences.zh: 他试图向各州传递一个信息。

sentences.en: Absolutely trying to send a message to the states.
sentences.zh: 绝对是在试图向各州传递信息。

sentences.en: But how would that actually work, though?
sentences.zh: 但那究竟会如何运作呢？

sentences.en: Because as you've explained to us, at this moment in time, a lot of the states have turned away from the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你向我们解释的那样，此时此刻，许多州已经抛弃了死刑。

sentences.en: So what practical effect does that message actually have?
sentences.zh: 那么这个信息实际上能产生什么实际效果呢？

sentences.en: To, you know, prosecutors have a lot of discretion in whether or not they're going to seek the death penalty in certain cases.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，检察官在某些案件中是否寻求死刑方面拥有很大的自由裁量权。

sentences.en: We talked about how expensive it is, what a hit, especially rural counties, take when they pursue it.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论过死刑有多昂贵，特别是在农村县份追求死刑时所受到的打击有多大。

sentences.en: And Trump was basically saying, go for it.
sentences.zh: 而特朗普基本上是在说，放手去做吧。

sentences.en: And how receptive were the states to this message?
sentences.zh: 各州对这一信息的接受度如何？

sentences.en: Overall, most states are really not engaging with death penalty in any significant way.
sentences.zh: 总体而言，大多数州并没有以任何实质性的方式参与死刑。

sentences.en: But I think there was a small cohort of states which had been implementing the death penalty that were open to this message.
sentences.zh: 但我认为有一小部分一直在实施死刑的州对这一信息持开放态度。

sentences.en: But the problem was one of how do you practically carry it out?
sentences.zh: 但问题在于如何实际执行。

sentences.en: This had become so difficult by this point because drug companies were heavily restricting or simply not making the drugs that were needed for lethal injection.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候，这已经变得非常困难，因为制药公司严重限制了或者干脆不生产致命注射所需的药物。

sentences.en: Because they were being pressured, public support waiting.
sentences.zh: 因为他们受到了压力，公众支持率在下降。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Not great business to be in the business of making execution drugs.
sentences.zh: 涉足死刑药物的生意并不是什么好生意。

sentences.en: And that's not the only problem.
sentences.zh: 这还不是唯一的问题。

sentences.en: The American Medical Association says physicians should not participate in executions.
sentences.zh: 美国医学会表示医生不应参与死刑执行。

sentences.en: So it's increasingly hard to find qualified people to carry these out.
sentences.zh: 因此，要找到合格的人员来执行这些死刑变得越来越困难。

sentences.en: And it becomes much more logistically challenging.
sentences.zh: 后勤挑战也变得更大。

sentences.en: So they're expensive.
sentences.zh: 所以它们很昂贵。

sentences.en: They're logistically much tougher.
sentences.zh: 在后勤上也棘手得多。

sentences.en: And, I mean, I feel like in the past few years is when we really started hearing about botched executions and sort of some of these grisly cases like Krista Pike.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，我觉得在过去的几年里，我们才真正开始听到关于行刑失误以及像克里斯塔·派克这样的一些可怕案件。

sentences.en: I think there have always been botched executions.
sentences.zh: 我想行刑失误一直都存在。

sentences.en: But we have been getting more news of this.
sentences.zh: 但我们现在听到的这方面的消息越来越多了。

sentences.en: And I think that has to do with the fact that as these drugs have gotten harder to get,
sentences.zh: 我认为这与以下事实有关：随着这些药物越来越难买到，

sentences.en: these states are often using either stockpiled expired drugs or they're using drugs that they had made at a compounding pharmacy.
sentences.zh: 这些州往往要么使用囤积的过期药物，要么使用他们从复合药房定制的药物。

sentences.en: And so you have this combination of it's very hard to get these drugs.
sentences.zh: 所以这就结合了多种情况：很难买到这些药物，

sentences.en: The drugs that these states do have are of uncertain quality.
sentences.zh: 这些州目前拥有的药物质量存疑，

sentences.en: And then it's harder and harder to get people to administer them who have a medical background.
sentences.zh: 而且越来越难找到具有医学背景的人来实施注射。

sentences.en: So for all of these reasons, states that may have even wanted to heed Trump's call are not perhaps able to or able to in the way that they would want.
sentences.zh: 因此，出于所有这些原因，即使是那些可能想要响应特朗普号召的州，也许也无法做到，或者无法按他们想要的方式做到。

sentences.en: Or they're trying and we're getting all these botched executions.
sentences.zh: 或者他们在尝试，结果我们看到了所有这些行刑失误。

sentences.en: But there is one state that really heeded the call.
sentences.zh: 但有一个州确实响应了号召。

sentences.en: Florida is quickly becoming the capital of capital punishment.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州正迅速成为死刑之都。

sentences.en: And that was Florida, starting in 2025.
sentences.zh: 那个州就是佛罗里达州，从 2025 年开始。

sentences.en: There are some crimes that are just so horrific, the only appropriate punishment is the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 有些罪行实在是太可怕了，唯一的适当惩罚就是死刑。

sentences.en: Governor Ron DeSantis started signing a flurry of death warrants.
sentences.zh: 罗恩·德桑蒂斯州长开始密集签署死刑令。

sentences.en: DeSantis signed a death warrant for a serial killer.
sentences.zh: 德桑蒂斯签署了一名连环杀手的死刑令。

sentences.en: Governor Ron DeSantis just signed the death warrant for Edward James.
sentences.zh: 罗恩·德桑蒂斯州长刚刚签署了爱德华·詹姆斯的死刑令。

sentences.en: But it is set to execute Polk County killer David Pittman.
sentences.zh: 但它定于处决波尔克县的杀手大卫·皮特曼。

sentences.en: Tonight, an Orange County man became the ninth person executed.
sentences.zh: 今晚，一名奥兰治县男子成为第九个被执行死刑的人。

sentences.en: He'll be the 12th execution in Florida.
sentences.zh: 他将是佛罗里达州第 12 个被执行死刑的人。

sentences.en: Record 19th execution.
sentences.zh: 创纪录的第 19 次死刑执行。

sentences.en: Governor Ron DeSantis has signed Florida's 20th death warrant of the year, putting the state on pace to set a new record for executions.
sentences.zh: 罗恩·德桑蒂斯州长签署了佛罗里达州今年的第 20 份死刑令，使该州的死刑执行速度有望创下新纪录。

sentences.en: He did so at such an extraordinary rate that last year, 19 men were executed.
sentences.zh: 他以如此惊人的速度推进，以至于去年有 19 名男子被处决。

sentences.en: That's 40 percent of the people who were executed in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这占去年美国被处决人数的 40%。

sentences.en: last year.
sentences.zh: 去年。

sentences.en: And this year, so far, Florida's executed more men than all other states combined.
sentences.zh: 而今年到目前为止，佛罗里达州处决的犯人数量已经超过了其他所有州的综合。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So what is Florida doing that other states seem either unwilling or unable to do that has allowed them to accelerate this so much?
sentences.zh: 那么佛罗里达州究竟在做什么，使得其他似乎不愿意或无法这样做的州相形见绌，从而让他们能够如此大幅度地加速死刑执行？

sentences.en: I think one thing is the very unusual setup that Florida has.
sentences.zh: 我认为其中一个原因是佛罗里达州非常特殊的体制设置。

sentences.en: So typically, a case works its way through the courts, and in a capital case, there are a number of appeals, and when those appeals are exhausted, a judge sets an execution date.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，案件会在法庭中审理，在死刑案件中，会有多次上诉，当这些上诉用尽时，法官会确定一个执行日期。

sentences.en: But in Florida, this works differently.
sentences.zh: 但在佛罗里达州，情况则有所不同。

sentences.en: There's one person in Florida who can sign death warrants, that being Governor Ron DeSantis, and this is unique among active death penalty states.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州只有一个人可以签署死刑令，那就是罗恩·德桑蒂斯州长，这在目前仍在实行死刑的各个州中是绝无仅有的。

sentences.en: Another thing is that there's no telling when or why he's going to choose who he chooses.
sentences.zh: 另一个原因是，你无法预知他将选择谁以及为什么要选择他们。

sentences.en: So there are men who are on Florida's death row right now who've been there since the 1970s who languish there,
sentences.zh: 因此，佛罗里达州死囚牢房里有些犯人自 20世纪 70 年代起就在那里度日如年，

sentences.en: while there are other men with much more recent convictions who have received these execution dates.
sentences.zh: 而另一些定罪时间要晚得多的人却收到了死刑执行日期。

sentences.en: We don't know how he's picking these men, is what you're saying.
sentences.zh: 你是说我们不知道他是如何挑选这些人的。

sentences.en: There is zero transparency.
sentences.zh: 完全没有任何透明度。

sentences.en: It's like in a black box how Governor DeSantis picks these men and why.
sentences.zh: 德桑蒂斯州长如何以及为何挑选这些人，就像在一个黑箱子里一样。

sentences.en: One victim's family was so frustrated with how many years the defendant had been awaiting the death penalty that they sent Governor DeSantis customized Sharpies.
sentences.zh: 一位受害者的家属对被告等待死刑的年数感到万分沮丧，以至于他们给德桑蒂斯州长寄去了定制的锋芒笔。

sentences.en: He signs his death warrants and other legislation and Sharpies, and the Sharpies were sent to him asking for him to sign a death warrant for the defendant in this case,
sentences.zh: 他用这种笔签署死刑令和其他立法，人们把笔寄给他，请求他为本案被告签署死刑令，

sentences.en: which Governor DeSantis subsequently did.
sentences.zh: 而德桑蒂斯州长随后确实这样做了。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: And in other states, typically, there's 90 days.
sentences.zh: 而在其他州，通常有 90 天的时间。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's much longer between when the death warrant is signed and when the execution actually takes place.
sentences.zh: 有时，死刑令签署和实际执行死刑之间的时间间隔要长得多。

sentences.en: Why that timeframe is so important is there are issues that have often not been litigated that suddenly you can litigate in the present day.
sentences.zh: 这个时间框架之所以如此重要，是因为往往有一些以前未曾诉讼过的问题，你突然可以在当下提出诉讼。

sentences.en: In Florida, you have a 30-day period in which to do this kind of work.
sentences.zh: 在佛罗里达州，你只有 30 天的时间来做这类工作。

sentences.en: So the chance for error is so great.
sentences.zh: 因此出错的几率非常高。

sentences.en: And this is an issue of particular concern in Florida, which holds the record for having the most death row exonerees, 30 in all.
sentences.zh: 这也是佛罗里达州一个特别令人担忧的问题，该州拥有拥有最多被平反的死囚犯的记录，总共 30 人。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So basically, they've removed a lot of the breaks that other states have in order to sort of speed up these executions.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，他们为了加快执行死刑的速度，取消了其他州所拥有的许多刹车机制。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And there are other things that have gone on in Florida as well, and that includes legislative efforts to make more crimes eligible for the death penalty,
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州还发生了一些其他事情，包括旨在让更多罪行适用死刑的立法努力，

sentences.en: also to allow for non-unanimous juries to vote for death.
sentences.zh: 还允许非一致陪审团投票判处死刑。

sentences.en: That means just eight jurors out of 12 are enough.
sentences.zh: 这意味着 12 名陪审员中只要有 8 名就足够了。

sentences.en: To recommend a death sentence.
sentences.zh: 来建议判处死刑。

sentences.en: And so these are all ways in which this is being expanded in Florida, but also it puts defendants at danger of not having the due process that they need.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些都是佛罗里达州扩大死刑的方式，但这同时也使被告面临失去所需正当程序的危险。

sentences.en: And just to give a sense of the pace of things, there are executions taking place in Florida typically at least once a month.
sentences.zh: 为了让人对死刑执行的节奏有个概念，佛罗里达州通常每个月至少会执行一次死刑。

sentences.en: There are four active death warrants right now, and there could be a double execution this coming Tuesday, October 13th.
sentences.zh: 目前有四个生效的死刑令，并且就在下周二，即 10 月 13 日，可能会有双重死刑执行。

sentences.en: Pam, you mentioned all these problems with drugs, for instance, finding drugs, finding medical professionals to administer the drugs.
sentences.zh: 帕姆，你提到了药物方面的所有这些问题，例如寻找药物，寻找医护人员来实施注射。

sentences.en: Is Florida just not having those problems, or are they just finding ways around them?
sentences.zh: 难道佛罗里达州就没有这些问题，还是他们只是找到了绕过这些问题的方法？

sentences.en: Like, why are they not encountering the same issues as other states?
sentences.zh: 比如说，为什么他们没有遇到与其他州相同的问题？

sentences.en: I think there's so many questions we don't know the answers to because of the black box nature of how this is done in Florida.
sentences.zh: 我想由于佛罗里达州这种操作黑箱化的性质，有太多问题我们都不知道答案。

sentences.en: They may have stockpiled drugs that are expired.
sentences.zh: 他们可能囤积了已经过期的药物。

sentences.en: We don't know the quality of those drugs.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道那些药物的质量如何。

sentences.en: We do know that one of them is a paralytic, which was not present in Tennessee, where Krista Pike was able to articulate that she felt her arm burning and was able to move.
sentences.zh: 我们确实知道其中一种是麻痹剂，这在田纳西州是没有的，当时克里斯塔·派克能够清楚表达她感到手臂灼痛并且能够移动。

sentences.en: So, when you introduce a paralytic, there are all sorts of new questions involved about how much that prisoner is suffering during the execution itself.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你引入麻痹剂时，就会产生各种各样的新问题，涉及囚犯在行刑过程中究竟经受了多少痛苦。

sentences.en: Because if they are suffering, the idea is they wouldn't be able to tell you or it might not be apparent.
sentences.zh: 因为如果他们在受苦，其用意就是他们无法告诉你，或者可能表现不出来。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: So, it depends how we're talking about botching, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这取决于我们如何定义行刑失误，对吧？

sentences.en: We can see some things and other things are more hidden.
sentences.zh: 有些事情我们能看到，而另一些事情则更加隐蔽。

sentences.en: And I think having covering this issue for a long time, I feel that it's inevitable that something will happen in Florida and other states like what we've seen in Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 我想报道这个问题很长时间后，我觉得佛罗里达州以及像田纳西州那样的事情迟早会发生。

sentences.en: This has to do with an aging prison population where it's harder to access a vein.
sentences.zh: 这与老龄化的监狱人口有关，在那里很难找到静脉注射。

sentences.en: Different states are experimenting with different drug protocols and different ways to do this.
sentences.zh: 不同的州正在尝试不同的药物方案和不同的执行方式。

sentences.en: So, I think what happened to Krista Pike is really a preview of what lays ahead.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为克里斯塔·派克身上发生的事情确实是未来情况的预演。

sentences.en: It feels sort of ironic, actually, because, as you explained to us, lethal injection was introduced because it was seen as the most humane way to execute somebody, right?
sentences.zh: 实际上这听起来有点讽刺，因为正如你向我们解释的那样，采用注射死刑是因为它被视为处决某人最人道的方式，对吧？

sentences.en: It was promoted as this humane solution compared to the electric chair or a firing squad or hanging, all of which have been used in this country.
sentences.zh: 与电椅、行刑队或绞刑——这些都曾在这个国家使用过——相比，它被宣传为人道的解决方案。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: When lethal injection was first introduced as a method of carrying out executions, I think part of the idea was to sanitize what was being done,
sentences.zh: 当注射死刑最初作为一种行刑方式被引入时，我想部分想法是为了掩盖正在做的事情，

sentences.en: which was the taking of a life by the state.
sentences.zh: 那就是国家剥夺一个人的生命。

sentences.en: And as lethal injection has failed more often, we're also seeing states moving toward things like firing squads and the electric chair.
sentences.zh: 而随着注射死刑更频繁地失效，我们也看到各州开始转向行刑队和电椅之类的方法。

sentences.en: Just last week, the likely next governor of Tennessee, Marsha Blackburn, said she wanted to bring back the electric chair.
sentences.zh: 就在上周，田纳西州可能上任的下届州长玛莎·布莱克本表示，她想恢复电椅死刑。

sentences.en: And one could argue that the electric chair or firing squads are more honest and more transparent about what is taking place.
sentences.zh: 人们可能会争辩说，电椅或行刑队对于正在发生的事情更加诚实、更加透明。

sentences.en: But states obviously take a risk when they carry out executions that way because it shows what they are doing in a way that a quiet act that is supposed to look like something medical does not.
sentences.zh: 但各州以这种方式执行死刑显然是在冒风险，因为它以一种看起来像医疗行为的安静举动所没有的方式，赤裸裸地展现了他们在做的事情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, on some level,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从某种程度上讲，

sentences.en: that does make sense because you're seeing something and maybe experiencing it in a more visceral way that really makes you kind of reckon with what's actually happening in front of you and the fact of death.
sentences.zh: 这确实说得通，因为你看到了某些东西，也许是以一种更深刻、更直观的方式去体验它，这真地会让你不得不认真思考眼前究竟在发生什么以及死亡这一事实。

sentences.en: And maybe for some people, that's fine.
sentences.zh: 也许对某些人来说，这没什么。

sentences.en: Half the population supports the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 有一半的人口支持死刑。

sentences.en: And so maybe for them, firing squads, the electric chair, none of that will be a problem.
sentences.zh: 所以对他们来说，行刑队、电椅，这些可能都不是问题。

sentences.en: But I would imagine for a lot of people, they just can't stomach that.
sentences.zh: 但我猜对很多人来说，他们就是无法接受。

sentences.en: Like, it might be going too far.
sentences.zh: 比如说，这可能太过分了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I often think about the fact that when I witnessed an execution in 1998 in Texas, it was as if I were watching someone go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我经常想起这件事：1998年在得克萨斯州目睹一场死刑时，感觉就像在看一个人睡着一样。

sentences.en: I think when we see Florida ramping up, when we see other states trying some of these, what we think of as sort of more barbaric ways to execute people,
sentences.zh: 我认为，当我们看到佛罗里达州在加码，当我们看到其他州在尝试一些我们认为是更野蛮的处决方式时，

sentences.en: it engenders a lot of bigger questions about where we're headed with the death penalty and whether this is about to peter out
sentences.zh: 这引发了许多关于我们死刑走向何方的大问题，以及这是否即将渐渐消亡，

sentences.en: because people will be so horrified by what they see or whether we're seeing a resurgence in these states that have clung so hard to the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 因为人们会对他们所看到的感到无比震惊，或者我们正在看到那些紧抓死刑不放的州迎来复苏。

sentences.en: Pam Koloff, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 帕姆·科洛夫，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Russian authorities said on Wednesday that a researcher at a Siberian anti-plague institute who died from a mysterious pneumonia
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯当局周三表示，西伯利亚一家反鼠疫研究所的一名研究员死于神秘肺炎，

sentences.en: had been vaccinated against the pathogens that she worked with and that no, quote, emergency situations had occurred at the lab.
sentences.zh: 她曾接种过所研究病原体的疫苗，实验室没有、引述“发生紧急情况”。

sentences.en: The statement from the Russian health regulator came after the U.S.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯卫生监管机构发表这一声明之前，美国

sentences.en: urged Moscow to be more forthcoming about the possible public health incident
sentences.zh: 敦促莫斯科方面更加坦诚地对待可能发生的公共卫生事件，

sentences.en: and after the World Health Organization asked for more information to make an accurate assessment of any threat.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，世界卫生组织也要求提供更多信息，以便对任何威胁作出准确评估。

sentences.en: The lack of on-site health investigators and the lack of details from Russian officials have fueled doubts about the Russian government's insistence
sentences.zh: 缺乏现场卫生调查人员以及俄罗斯官员缺乏细节，加剧了人们对俄罗斯政府坚称

sentences.en: that it has the situation under control.
sentences.zh: 它已控制住局势的怀疑。

sentences.zh: 今天的节目由奥利维亚·纳特、阿德里安娜·赫斯特、杰西卡·钟和埃里克·克鲁普克制作。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一个被严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了群自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱且有时激动人心的斗争中。
